title: Conditional Poincare-before-Duhamel shell transport
question: Can the nonnegative Doob shell variance from R-398 be converted shell by shell into a conditional Dirichlet energy divided by a measurable birth-death spectral gap, replacing the unresolved direct shell estimate by two separately testable inputs?
method: Rebuild the registered finite Q3 quartic oscillator chain and the Gibbs/history coordinate distributions on the complete R-398 volume/cutoff grid.

For every oriented prefix, form the conditional reference law pi_a and conditional likelihood f_a; compute the ordered-level birth-death conductance Laplacian and its first nonzero generalized eigenvalue lambda_a.
Evaluate the shell conditional variance, the nearest-neighbour Dirichlet energy, the Poincare bound D/lambda, and both unweighted and exp(2 mu r)-weighted transfers.
Rebuild all aggregates in a non-importing independent lane, remove the gap denominator and conditional parent in a hostile lane, and compile the scalar transfer skeleton in Lean R399.
Retain finite gap and gradient profiles as diagnostics only; do not infer a thermodynamic lower bound or real-time decay theorem.
finding: The finite transfer is valid on all 3,584 oriented actual-Q3 history contexts. The primary lane passes 8,975/8,975 assertions, the independent lane reproduces the aggregate fields, the hostile lane passes 5/5, the integrated verifier passes 31/31, and Lean R399 compiles. The minimum conditional birth-death gap is 0.49325229280535315; maximum shell variance is 0.00021579891795778293; maximum mu=1/8 weighted shell variance is 0.00031475936144631414; maximum Poincare shell bound is 0.00031370151228040375; maximum weighted Poincare shell bound is 0.00045782017814794144; and maximum weighted transfer residual is 0.00014306081670162753. Removing the gap denominator produces a selected-context deficit 2.7443920018295422e-05, while an unconditional-parent mutation mismatches the shell energy by 0.000112174 and is caught.
decision_reason: R-399 supplies a distinct conditional-information-to-Dirichlet interface. It turns each R-398 shell variance into a local gradient budget divided by an explicit finite conditional gap, so the remaining analytic problem is split into a gap theorem and a gradient-decay theorem. The finite minimum is calibration only; cutoff/volume/source/phase uniformity and real-time decay remain open.

adversarial_review.check: The hostile lane drops the spectral-gap denominator and obtains a deficit above threshold, so the Poincare factor cannot be omitted.
An unconditional parent likelihood is compared with the genuine Doob parent and the mismatch is above threshold.
The conductance form is explicitly declared; changing the local Dirichlet form changes the gate and is not silently identified with the physical Q3 generator.
The minimum gap is retained per system and is not promoted to cutoff-, volume-, source- or phase-uniform positivity.
The coordinate gradient profile is finite bookkeeping and is not called a Lieb-Robinson or common-core estimate.
The independent lane reconstructs the Q3 system, Gibbs states, histories, conditional laws and spectral gaps without importing the primary route module.
Phase conditioning, folded Euclidean domination, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Prove or refute a phase-conditioned lower bound on the same conditional Dirichlet gap and a source-, volume-, cutoff- and shape-uniform decay estimate for the actual likelihood gradients, in both orientations and adjoints. If the gap collapses under increasing-cutoff stress, retain R-398 and register the conditional-Poincare obstruction.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite conditional Poincare and shell-gradient diagnostic. No uniform conditional gap, gradient decay, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure follows.
no_overclaim: The finite Poincare inequality is an exact change of bookkeeping. A positive finite gap is not a thermodynamic lower bound, and the discrete coordinate gradient is not a real-time Lieb-Robinson estimate.
